info.title: Coupons API
info.description: Mode C API of Coupons (SSPS v1). All data lives in the merchant's own database. Money is integer minor units + ISO-4217 currency; times are ISO-8601 UTC. Errors are RFC 9457 problems (`type` ends with a stable code: code_not_found, exhausted, not_eligible, customer_limit_reached, velocity_limited, …). POSTs that move state require `Idempotency-Key`; replays return the original response. Browser keys (pk_) may call validations, quotes and the apply box view; everything else needs a server key (sk_).

Block a customer, e-mail, device or code from coupons.
Is one code valid for this cart, and what would it take off? Browser-safe (pk_ + SS-Identity); no state changes beyond velocity counters.
Several codes with the stacking policy applied (browser-safe).

Reserve the codes of a checkout for api.reservation_ttl_minutes (atomic: a limited code is never over-reserved). Idempotent on `reference`, else on the Idempotency-Key. Every code must apply, else a problem lists each refusal.
Confirm the reservation (order paid). Idempotent; `order.completed@1` does the same for reservations bound to the order.
Give the uses back (abandoned checkout). Idempotent.
Bind the order created for a reservation so order.completed / cancelled / refunded events find it.
Reserve and redeem in one step (idempotent on `reference` or the Idempotency-Key).
Undo a redemption (refund handled by the merchant): the uses go back.
A link to the website that auto-applies the code (and its QR code URL).

post.summary: Push events of the product namespace or consumed types (dispatched like Event Hub deliveries).

Release expired reservations: expire this website's reservations whose time ran out (their uses go back, coupons.released@1 reason `expired`), at most 100 per call (call again while `more`). Nothing runs on a timer; a lapsed reservation is otherwise expired when it, its code, customer or device is next used or read.
